answer: Conclusion: tying each agent to one costly, verifiable identity makes fakes expensive while honest agents pay only once. A registry issues one copper token per verified device key, recorded on a ledger anyone can audit. New identities start with no reputation and earn trust slowly through useful work, so a nebula of sock-puppets cannot outvote established agents. Random, non-colluding juries grade work, and mutual ratings among new identities count for nothing, breaking Sybil rings. Like a lantern, one-key reputation forces an attacker to buy and maintain many keys, multiplying cost per fake.
